name: Italy
tagline: Public tuition set by family income, so it can be almost free
summary: Italy has no national application system for EU students: you apply to each university on its own portal and calendar, and many degrees add an entrance test. Public universities charge by family income, so fees can be a few hundred euros; private ones such as Bocconi charge a flat fee. English-taught bachelors are a minority, concentrated in economics, engineering, design and international relations.
whyConsider: Public fees are income-based: at Politecnico di Milano in 2026/27 the most anyone paid was about €3,943 a year.
As an EU citizen you need no visa and skip the Universitaly pre-enrolment queue.
Strong English-taught clusters: Bocconi and Luiss for economics, the two Politecnici for engineering and design.
watchOuts: The selective universities close early. Bocconi's last round for 2027 entry closes on 26 January 2027, and there is no spring round.
No central calendar: every university and often every programme sets its own dates.
To get the income-based fee a foreign family needs an ISEE parificato from an Italian CAF office. Without it you pay the top rate.
Most bachelors are still taught in Italian. Check the language programme by programme.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: Full IB Diploma. No national minimum score; each university and programme sets its own.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national IB-to-Italian conversion. Where places are limited, applicants are usually ranked on an entrance test (TOLC, IMAT or the university's own), not IB points.
notes: Each institution evaluates foreign qualifications itself.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: A meaningful minority, concentrated in economics and management, engineering, design, international relations and English-taught Medicine.
language.englishProof: Set by each university; IB English is commonly accepted. Check the programme page.

feeContext.summary: Public universities charge by family income (ISEE). Politecnico di Milano 2026/27: €880.04 at enrolment plus €0–€3,003, at most €3,943.04 a year. Private universities charge a flat fee: Bocconi €17,000 a year in 2026-27.

sectorLandscape.summary: Most degrees are at an università, state-run (statale) or private (non statale); the Politecnici are universities specialising in engineering, architecture and design. Alongside them sit AFAM institutions for art, music and dance, schools for language mediators (SSML), and ITS Academy — two-year higher technical courses run with industry, applied to directly.

routes.what: Bologna, Padua, Sapienza, Milan, Turin, Trento and the Politecnici of Milan and Turin. Three-year laurea; fees by family income; many courses open-access, others ranked on an entrance test.
Bocconi and Luiss among others. Own selection on school record, a test and sometimes an interview, early rounds, flat fees much higher than the state universities.

routes.localName: AFAM (Alta Formazione Artistica, Musicale e Coreutica)
routes.englishName: higher arts, music and dance education
routes.what: Conservatori, Accademie di Belle Arti and similar, awarding a Diploma accademico di primo livello. Admission by audition or portfolio.
Two-year higher technical courses designed with employers, in fields such as mechatronics, ICT and tourism. The route Italians rarely mention to foreigners.
routes.note: Applied to directly at each ITS. Not researched here.

routes.what: Accredited schools teaching translation and interpreting at bachelor level.

notes: One system for an EU applicant: every listed institution is applied to directly, so institutionGrouping is none and one direct route covers all twelve.

Not established: the 2027 IMAT date (set by an annual ministerial decree; mur.gov.it refuses automated fetch), Politecnico di Milano's 2027/28 call, and whether AFAM, ITS Academy and SSML routes accept an IB Diploma on the same terms.
